title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Pet and house sitting
audience: Pet and house sitters who want to move from a per-visit or per-day price to a clear offer for the owner's home.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will look after your dogs while you are away' describes a service. 'I will stay in your home for five nights, visit the dogs at set times each day, send a photo and a note after each visit, and bring in a named substitute if I am unwell' is an offer. The owner buys the result and the certainty of getting it, including the care of the home while they are away.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a sitting offer
instruction.body: Name the outcome: the animals fed, walked and settled, and the home secure at the end of each day. Set the time frame: the dates, the visit times and the handover. List what the owner must do: provide food, medication instructions, emergency vet authority and access. Add a certainty element, such as a daily photo and report. State the risk you carry, such as a named substitute and what your insurance covers. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Packages that step up
instruction.body: Vendor price guides show different levels of care. Dogster's table, which is headed per dog per day, lists at-home visits and walks at $25 to $45, overnight stays at a sitter's home at $45 to $80, and house sitting at $60 to $100 (vendor, 4 July 2026, updated 18 October 2026). The same article also gives dog sitting as around $80 to $150 a day, which conflicts with its own at-home row. Use these only as a rough market check, and set your price from your costs. Three levels work well: visits only; an overnight stay in your home; and house sitting with a daily report and a named substitute. Jobber describes stepped packages in which each higher level adds something the customer can see (updated 8 October 2024).

instruction.heading: Guarantees, claims and the total
instruction.body: Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services and cannot be removed by a contract term. Do not claim that your sitting keeps animals calmer or healthier unless you can substantiate it. Show one total and say whether GST applies, as Western Australia's consumer agency asks (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). A workmanship promise you choose to add sits on top of the consumer guarantees (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). Written permission to hold keys and enter the home is a practice point; this research found no Australian rule on key holding.

instruction.heading: Price on value, then check cost
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, check the price against your cost per hour and visit time, and then decide on any premium. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). Victorian rules for in-home pet sitting are unresolved in this research. Victoria's boarding code defines a boarding establishment as one that cares for cats and dogs for owners away from home, but the source does not say whether that covers animals in a sitter's own home. Ask the council before you describe your Victorian service as a boarding service.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence an owner would repeat, such as 'your animals are fed, walked and settled, and your home is secure each day'.
Set the dates and visit times, and check them against how you have met such times before.
List what the owner provides, such as food, medication notes, vet authority and access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a daily photo and report.
Decide the cover for an absence, and check that you can afford it and that your insurance responds.
Price from value, check against cost and visit time, and state one total with GST status.

workedExamples.situation: A sitter in Melbourne is offered a five-night house sit for two dogs, with visits twice a day, through an online platform. The owner asks whether she can do it for a single daily rate and wants a photo each day. The sitter currently quotes per visit and sends no report.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer, then decide how to show the price for the stay.
workedExamples.reasoning: She writes the offer as one stay with a daily photo, a logbook and a named substitute if she cannot attend. Dogster's vendor table lists at-home visits and walks at $25 to $45 per dog per day, and overnight stays at $45 to $80 per dog (4 July 2026, updated 18 October 2026). Its table is headed per dog per day, so the unit of the overnight row must be confirmed before she uses it as a per-night figure. She prices the stay from her own cost and visit time, states one total with GST status, and treats any platform fee as a cost, because the platform takes a share of each booking. Because no Australian source for key holding was found, she gets written permission for keys and entry as a practice step.

equipmentAndPpe: Written offer with the levels, the dates and the exclusions
Daily report template with a photo and short notes
Logbook for feeding, medication and visits
Written permission for keys and home access, dated (a practice point, not a sourced legal rule)

commonErrors.error: Quoting a per-visit price with no outcome, so the owner compares on price alone
commonErrors.prevention: Write the outcome, the visit times and the daily report into the offer.

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee you cannot afford to honour, such as cover for any absence
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the cover to a named substitute and to what your insurance covers.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate, such as a calmer pet
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have recorded.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check the rules where the work is done before you describe your offer as a boarding service.

Victoria: the boarding establishment code covers businesses that care for cats and dogs for owners away from home, and boarding businesses register as Domestic Animal Businesses with their council. The research did not show whether the code covers animals kept in a sitter's own home. Victorian in-home pet sitting rules are UNRESOLVED. Ask the council before advising.
The Australian Consumer Law applies to pricing statements, and misleading price statements are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

A broker source says no regulation currently requires pet sitters to hold specific insurance, and recommends public liability cover (Marsh, no date shown). Check that your policy covers animals in a client's home.

qualityStandard: Each offer states the outcome, dates, visit times, owner duties, one total price with GST status and the exclusions.
The price is checked against cost, visit time and any platform fee.
Each guarantee is one the sitter can deliver and insure.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with the levels, dates and exclusions
Price check showing cost, visit time, platform fee and margin
Daily report and logbook for each stay
Written permission for keys and home access, with the date
summary: A good sitting offer promises an outcome, with dates, visit times, a daily report and a named substitute.
Vendor rates are a rough guide, and one vendor article conflicts with itself, so confirm your own price.
Victorian in-home rules are unresolved, so ask the council before you describe your home as a boarding service.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a house-sitting offer does the owner buy?
options: Your car, your kit and your phone
How many years you have been sitting

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a guarantee on a sitting offer be?
options: Unlimited, with no limit on what it covers
Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for owners who are your friends
Something you can deliver and afford

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a claim such as 'your pet stays calmer' have?
options: A famous endorsement from a celebrity
A discount on the next stay
